correctness.rationale: PASS: Fix a>=b>=1 and palette k=b+2. Greedily color universal vertex u with its favorite; process b vertices of side B assigning favorite of remaining colors; color all of A with the sole remaining color. Every envy arc points to an earlier colored vertex, including the full-arc definition in the pinned text; in Koana-Oh-Yoneda’s adjacency-only envy graph this is only easier. For k=b+1 when b>=2, choose b indexed vertices on each side whose favorite i (1<=i<=b) and second favorite k produce, after excluding ANY one color used on u, a complete set of favorite remaining colors in both sides. Every proper coloring has disjoint nonempty color sets S_A,S_B. For each s in S_A a B vertex assigned f(s) in S_B prefers s; for each t in S_B an A vertex assigned g(t) in S_A prefers t. A cycle of g∘f on the finite S_A gives a directed alternating envy cycle; every arc joins A and B, so is an actual edge also under the paper’s stricter official definition. Distinct colors on that orbit force distinct witness vertices. If b=1 the graph contains a triangle, giving 3. Fresh exhaustively enumerated all proper (b+1)-colorings for (a,b)=(2,2),(3,2),(3,3): respectively 6,6,168 proper, zero stable, corroborating the construction without proving all parameters. Potential wording difference: pinned RESULT defines envy arcs between any two vertices whereas original arXiv defines only between adjacent vertices; both bounds actually hold under adjacency-restricted definition, so the asserted numerical invariant survives.
